title: Soils and Natural Vegetation: India's Living Cover

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the five soil-forming factors?
questions.rationale: The five factors are parent rock, climate, relief, organisms, and time — colour is a result, not a cause.

questions.question: Alluvial soils cover roughly what share of India's area?
questions.rationale: Alluvial soils — the khadar and bhangar of the northern plains and coasts — cover about 43% of India's land.

questions.question: Black (regur) soil has formed mainly from:
questions.rationale: Black soil is the weathered product of Deccan Trap basalt — clay-rich, moisture-retentive, and ideal for cotton.

questions.question: Khadar differs from bhangar in that khadar is:
questions.rationale: Khadar is the new alluvium renewed by floods; bhangar is the older, higher alluvium with lime kankar nodules.

questions.question: Tea, coffee, and cashew grow best on which heavily leached soil?
questions.rationale: Laterite, leached in the high-rainfall Ghats and hills, suits plantation crops such as tea, coffee, cashew, and rubber.

questions.question: The ravines of the Chambal valley are a textbook example of:
questions.rationale: Runoff carving deep channels has dissected the Chambal valley into badland gullies.

questions.question: Ploughing with furrows running across, instead of down, a slope is called:
questions.rationale: Contour ploughing makes each furrow a small dam that slows runoff across the slope, cutting erosion.

questions.question: Tropical evergreen forests in India require rainfall above:
questions.rationale: Evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, north-east, and Andamans thrive above 200 cm of rain; thorn scrub survives below 75 cm.

questions.question: Which vegetation type is India's most widespread?
questions.rationale: Tropical deciduous forest — home of teak and sal — covers the widest area, shedding leaves during the long dry season.

questions.question: India's first biosphere reserve, set up in 1986, was:
questions.rationale: The Nilgiri biosphere reserve of 1986 was the first of India's 18 reserves; Project Tiger began in 1973 and Jim Corbett National Park in 1936.
